learning_outcomes.text: Understand the practice for developing pneumatic and hydraulic circuits in industrial environments.
Master the generation, transport, and application of energy stored in a fluid to transform it into mechanical energy.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and their application to solving problems in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels, and fluid systems.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, labor plans, and other similar works.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technology Engineer.
Identifies and knows the functionality of the elements that are part of pneumatic and hydraulic circuits, as well as their standardized representations.
Is capable of designing a pressure fluid generation and distribution network, for both oil and air.
Can analyze the operation of a pneumatic or hydraulic circuit.
Is capable, based on the knowledge of the mechanical work to be performed, of designing a pneumatic and hydraulic circuit to carry it out, both intuitively and systematically.

syllabus_topics: Characteristics and uses of Hydraulics and Pneumatics.
Direction control, pressure regulation, and flow regulation.
Introduction of auxiliary elements participating in circuits.
How to approach a design, whether intuitive or systematic.
Systematic sequential design. Cascade and step-by-step memory structure.
Operating diagrams of valves, flow rates, positions, and volumes.
assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation, case resolution accounts for 2/3 of the final grade and practical reports for 1/3. A minimum grade of 3 out of 10 is required for each part. Students not completing continuous assessment can opt for global evaluation, which consists of a written test (2/3 of the grade) and a practical test (1/3 of the grade), with a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 required for each. Use of unpermitted materials during evaluation tests may lead to withdrawal from the exam and a grade of 0.
